newsitem.title: UK: Minor metals - Slow, opinions divided on antimony.
newsitem.headline: Minor metals - Slow, opinions divided on antimony.

text.p: Minor metals remained handcuffed to tight ranges over the past week as the market continued to slumber in the traditionally slow summer period, traders said on Thursday.
Drifting antimony divided trader opinion on its near-term direction, while another bout of downside pricing took the edge off last weeks recovery in Russian cobalt.
Elsewhere, vanadium firmed against the backdrop of tight physical supplies.
A drying up of Chinese offers, rains in China, slow consumer demand and talk of ample supplies helped to contribute to strongly divided opinions on antimony's next move.
The only outright agreement reached by traders asked by Reuters was that conditions remained thin, with only small pockets of business being concluded.
"Its like pointing your bellows at a dead barbeque," one trader said on antimony.

The bullish side of the equation argued that the monsoon season in China was affecting shipments of antimony from the worlds largest producer. They also said production of the metal used in batteries, solders and as a flame retardant when in oxide form has dropped following recent low market prices.
"It is not viable for some Chinese producers to keep their facilities open in the current climate...this is helping to reduce stock levels," one trader said.

Others said there was enough stock stored in Rotterdam to meet consumer demand during the slow summer period and that prices were set to fall near-term. "There will be no recovery in prices until at least September," one trader said.
Pricing operations helped to cap last weeks snap higher in Russian cobalt, though traders believed that prices would soon absorb the pressure following recent brisk consumer demand.
"There is plenty of demand out there which will eventually push prices higher," one trader commented.

Scant prompt material moved vanadium in a thin market. Traders said low production from China and Russia was helping to underpin the market, though one noted that one South African producer was looking to raise output.
Bismuth drifted back, though underlying demand remained robust, while indium showed signs of moving higher after recent downside pressure.
